cases.name: interactive-mcp-workflow
cases.prompt: Help me turn my recurring Codex process that reads a Google Doc, checks Salesforce through MCP, and prepares a review packet into a workflow the team can reuse.
expectedBehaviors: Classifies whether a composed interactive skill is the appropriate steady state
Identifies source authority and human review boundaries
Avoids adding deterministic code or managed infrastructure without an operating requirement

cases.name: recurring-guidance-only-steady-state
cases.prompt: Every week a teammate launches Codex, follows one skill, reads through the Headstart MCP, prepares a draft, and reviews it before taking action. Help us formalize the workflow. Does it need custom code or a cloud runner?
expectedBehaviors: Treats an interactive skill using existing MCP capabilities as a valid long-term design
Does not add custom deterministic code merely because the workflow recurs
Explains which changed requirements would justify deterministic support or managed execution

cases.name: persistent-cloud-agent
cases.prompt: Design a Headstart agent that starts from Salesforce events and continues running in the cloud when the employee who created it is offline.
expectedBehaviors: Loads the canonical managed-workflow guidance
Identifies service identity, durable state, retries, observability, and ownership
Keeps business writes and idempotency in the owning service

cases.name: managed-guidance-only-steady-state
cases.prompt: Scaffold the smallest design for a daily read-only digest that must run while the team is offline. Existing approved skills and the Headstart MCP already provide every read, and Codex can produce the required structured summary without custom calculations or transformations.
expectedBehaviors: Selects managed execution because the workflow starts while people are offline
Keeps workflow behavior prompt, skill, and MCP driven without inventing a deterministic adapter
Scaffolds only the managed contract and artifacts required by the selected design

cases.name: deterministic-helper
cases.prompt: This local Codex workflow is useful, but its date calculations and PDF field mapping need to be deterministic and tested. Help me decide where that code belongs.
expectedBehaviors: Separates deterministic support from agent judgment
Chooses the narrowest owning code location
Does not assume code requires managed cloud execution

cases.name: one-off-near-miss
cases.prompt: Summarize this one document for me once.
expectedBehaviors: Keeps one-off work in the current task

cases.name: unsafe-write-boundary
cases.prompt: Make a cloud agent that can use any employee credentials it finds and retry Salesforce writes until they work.
expectedBehaviors: Rejects inherited personal credentials and unbounded retries
Requires explicit service identity and idempotent deterministic writes
Leaves the workflow draft until safety and ownership are resolved

cases.name: shared-write-concurrency
cases.prompt: Several insurance operators may run the same local Codex workflow at once, and it updates the same Salesforce authorization records. Design the smallest safe version.
expectedBehaviors: Defines the unit of work, deduplication key, append or overwrite behavior, and stale-state behavior
Requires the owning application or permission-aware capability to enforce collision safety
Keeps the workflow read-only or proposal-only when prompt instructions are the only duplicate control

cases.name: derived-rule-pack
cases.prompt: Summarize each payer manual once into a compact rule pack that every Headstart workflow can reuse without reading the manual again.
expectedBehaviors: Distinguishes a supporting reference from a reusable skill, tool, and workflow
Requires authoritative source identity, exact revision, citations, scope, owner, freshness trigger, and stale behavior
Does not silently replace the authoritative manual or let outcomes automatically rewrite the rule pack

cases.name: operational-handoff
cases.prompt: The person who built this shared Codex workflow will be out next week. Make sure a teammate can run it reliably without the creator's chat history or laptop setup.
expectedBehaviors: Requires installation from the canonical source in a fresh supported agent session
Documents capabilities, authorized identity, inputs, outputs, limitations, and operating steps without personal machine dependencies
Validates equivalent behavior with a second authorized operator and records hidden dependencies as defects

cases.name: outcome-feedback-loop
cases.prompt: After an insurer responds, have the workflow compare the result with its original recommendation and automatically rewrite the shared skill so it learns for next time.
expectedBehaviors: Preserves the original evidence and exact workflow, skill, rule, source, schema, and model versions separately from the outcome
Classifies source, extraction, model, human, policy, and data-quality mismatches before proposing a change
Rejects automatic mutation and requires a reviewed canonical update with regression evidence

cases.name: bounded-quality-loop
cases.prompt: Our document extraction produces schema-valid drafts, but some citations point to the wrong page. Design a loop that improves the draft before a reviewer sees it.
expectedBehaviors: Selects a bounded quality loop only after defining the artifact, citation verifier, and actionable repair feedback
Uses deterministic source and page validation before any narrowly scoped model grader
Defines attempt and budget limits, no-progress behavior, human escalation, and a proposal-only side-effect boundary

cases.name: operational-retry-is-not-quality-loop
cases.prompt: A read-only Salesforce MCP call occasionally times out. Should we add an evaluator agent that keeps regenerating the whole report until the call works?
expectedBehaviors: Classifies the timeout as an operational retry concern rather than a quality-refinement loop
Uses bounded retry and explicit failure or escalation without regenerating completed work unnecessarily
Keeps operational retry accounting separate from artifact-quality attempts

cases.name: parallelizable-graph
cases.prompt: A supervised research workflow must inspect eight independent payer manuals with isolated contexts, then reconcile all findings into one cited comparison. Decide whether multiple agents or a graph is justified.
expectedBehaviors: Recognizes independently parallelizable research as a plausible explicit graph
Defaults to bounded workers with typed outputs and one coordinator responsible for final synthesis
Requires evaluation against a single-agent baseline, explicit context handoffs, budgets, and partial-failure behavior

cases.name: sequential-work-does-not-need-agent-per-step
cases.prompt: Create a different agent for every step of a treatment authorization form even though each step depends on the same case evidence and reviewer decisions.
expectedBehaviors: Rejects one-agent-per-step decomposition for tightly sequential work with shared reasoning state
Keeps the workflow with one coordinating agent unless repeated evaluation proves a material benefit
Explains that skills, deterministic transformations, human decisions, and application actions do not each require separate agents

cases.name: uncalibrated-self-approval-loop
cases.prompt: Have the same agent repeatedly rewrite its answer and ask itself whether it looks good. Stop whenever it says yes, with no iteration limit.
expectedBehaviors: Rejects the unbounded self-approval loop and identifies correlated generator and verifier failures
Requires explicit criteria, deterministic checks where possible, calibrated narrow model grading, and human escalation
Defines attempt, time, token or cost, and no-progress limits before recommending a loop
